findings.issue: The prose count 'six business days before the FOMC' is stale for the October cycle: Oct 2 to the Oct 27-28 FOMC is sixteen to seventeen business days (16 as of the Oct 27 meeting start, 17 as of the Oct 28 decision, excluding the Oct 12 holiday). The count was exact for the September cycle (Sep 4 -> Sep 15 = 6 business days excluding Labor Day) and has now survived one rebuild: the 2026-09-29 round-3 review logged this same nit as minor ('None blocking; do not rebuild solely for this'), and this fresh daily recollection still carries it. The endpoint dates in the same sentences are correct, and no rate, price, level or position size derives from the count.
findings.evidence: Python enumeration of weekdays between 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-27/28 excluding Oct 12 = 16 / 17 (command output, this review run). Prior record: fed-boc-watcher/review/2026-09-29/iteration-03/pm-review.json, approved, single minor finding on the same phrase ('In the next natural rebuild, change the count to sixteen business days (or drop it); do not rebuild solely for this.'). Present occurrences in this candidate: largest_pnl_risks[1] '...Oct 2 payrolls lands six business days before the FOMC.'; banks.fed.next_catalysts[1] '2026-10-02 08:30 Toronto - U.S. Employment Situation (September). First hard-activity print of the window, six business days before the FOMC.'
findings.pnl_impact: None blocking: every date, rate and price surrounding these sentences is correct; a reader could be mildly misled about how close the payrolls print sits to the FOMC, not about any market level or position size.
findings.instruction: In the next natural rebuild (or any batch of edits), change the count to 'sixteen business days' or drop it; do not rebuild or hold publication solely for this - but do apply it, since the same note went unfixed through the rebuild that followed it.

pnl_risks: FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again (no single-meeting distribution in this or the two prior daily snapshots): ZQV26 96.110 is an October monthly-average EFFR, not Oct 28 odds - re-price the Tuesday marks by hand before sizing any front-end position.

CRAU26's quote side (97.6225/97.6275; no last print, volume 0) is an indicative two-decimal spread implying ~2.375% quarterly average CORRA across both the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions; it cannot be decomposed into either and is not a verified executable price.

Data-wall risk with no bound consensus (fxstreet 401): today's 08:30 ET double release (Q2 GDP third estimate plus August PCE) and Friday's payrolls can each reprice the front end; the pre-committed thresholds (ZQV26 outside 96.00-96.25; payrolls vs the 3.890% no-move pricing) are the only falsifiers.

The dovish JOLTS increment (weight 0.5) is one release from a low base: a rebound in the next JOLTS print unwinds it with no Fed action at all, and the BoC hawkish column is empty by absence, not by evidence.

Frame expiry: both decisions land within four weeks and the average contracts can reprice on December without the Fed moving; by Oct 9 (Michigan preliminary, Canada LFS) the missing FedWatch pricing becomes a view on the data itself.
